In Tiny Glade, a small building is placed in front of an existing tower. Watch the building's actual shape change as its roof and walls are adjusted.

The building's geometry is what changed here. A change in its appearance on screen does not mean that the pixels themselves changed aspect ratio.

In our explanatory model, we now keep the building unchanged and change only the viewing direction. Distinguish the reveal of a previously hidden side from an edit to the building itself.

The view of a completed Townscaper building turns upward from a low angle. This time we exclude building edits and focus on the changing viewing direction.

First observe the Townscaper view in which the whole town appears small. Choose a roof corner as a reference and follow that point as the view moves closer.

This time watch the large Townscaper doorway and the roofs behind it together. The buildings remain unchanged as the view moves closer and then changes direction.

In the explanatory model on the right, we also mark the front wall and the roof behind it separately. Keeping the same reference points lets us compare an object edit with a change in viewing conditions.

As the model changes from a wide view to a close view, track both the front surface and the roof behind it. This reveals relationships that are easy to miss when watching only one object.
